segment: Courier-side B2B: LA businesses that put two-wheel couriers on the road (Chinese-language delivery platforms, Koreatown in-house delivery companies, courier e-bike rental operators, gig-platform vehicle marketplaces, pizza franchisees, other in-house courier crews)
summary: Research completed 2026-09-09 (9 web searches, 7 page fetches). The honest finding is that LA has NO branded courier e-bike rental fleet today: Zoomo's own /us/plans-los-angeles page now shows only NYC plans and one NYC store; Whizz's July-2026 city list is NYC, NJ, Philadelphia, DC, Chicago, SF (no LA); DoorDash's bike-dashing partner page names Dirwin (national purchase discount), Whizz and Swobbee but never mentions LA; a Spanish-language search finds only tourist rentals in Santa Monica. That is a supply gap HMP can fill, but it is a gap because the LA two-wheel courier pool is thin (~740 in the core zone per context), not because nobody tried. On the buyer side, none of the courier businesses found is a confirmed 10-50-unit purchaser: Fantuan and HungryPanda both cover LA and recruit riders there, but I could NOT confirm the earlier agent's claim that Fantuan rents e-bikes to LA riders (no public program page; the one documented LA Fantuan rider shipped his own Ninebot from China); HungryPanda publishes a partnerships email (business@hungrypanda.co) and offers rider 'care boxes', not vehicles. JQS Delivery (Koreatown, since 2010, 213-905-0441) is a real in-house delivery agency but publishes nothing about vehicles or fleet size; Koreatown delivery agencies appear car-based. Domino's LA franchisees post bring-your-own-bike 'Delivery Biker' jobs; the corporate e-bike program used Rad Power Bikes (2019) and the Benzina Zero HAULeR approval (2024) applies to Domino's Pizza Enterprises (Australia/NZ), not US franchisees, so a US franchisee buying a non-approved brand is unlikely. Product fit: INNO (Class 2, no license) is the only realistic courier product; FLASH/MK.II need an M1 license, registration and insurance that most gig couriers lack, so courier-side demand for them is near zero. Most realistic path is not a fleet PO but a channel listing (DoorDash 'Dasher Deals' via eco-doordash@doordash.com, HungryPanda/Fantuan rider-perk partnerships) that drives individual rider purchases/rentals at 768 Ceres Ave, plus small (2-10 unit) buys from Koreatown/SGV delivery agencies once vehicles are verified by site visit.

key_facts.claim: Zoomo's /us/plans-los-angeles page lists only NYC plans (Zoomo Zero from $39/week; $20/week Uber Eats rate; Premium dual-battery $65/week; purchase $790) and one US store at 252 W 38th St, New York; no Los Angeles store, hours or prices appear. LA operations are effectively closed/not listed.

Whizz's DoorDash e-bike rental guide (published 2026-06-16, updated 2026-07-22) lists Whizz cities as New York City, New Jersey, Philadelphia, Washington DC, Chicago and San Francisco; Los Angeles is not a Whizz city. DoorDash promos: up to $250 off first five months in Chicago/DC/SF/Philadelphia; 15% code 15DD in NYC/NJ.

DoorDash's Bike Dashing page names three vehicle partners: Dirwin (20% off purchase + free shipping/assembly, national), Whizz (15% off rental/rent-to-own; NYC, SF, DC, Philadelphia, Chicago, Jersey City), Swobbee (50% off 3-month battery-swap subscription; NYC, Jersey City). Los Angeles is not mentioned. The page gives one partner contact: eco-doordash@doordash.com ('businesses interested in connecting with the Bike Dasher community'). No formal application form exists.

Dirwin runs its own 'Delivery Partnerships' page: active Dashers register with their DoorDash account to unlock up to $500 off a Dirwin e-bike. This is the template for how a purchase-discount vendor gets listed with DoorDash (vendor-hosted verification form + DoorDash listing).

Uber's Vehicle Marketplace (uber.com/us/en/drive/vehicle-solutions) is a car rental/purchase marketplace for drivers; the only two-wheel partner found is Zenion electric mopeds in the UK (GBP 75/week with battery swaps). No LA two-wheel vendor is listed. Uber Eats LA courier signup requires the courier to own a bicycle/e-bike/scooter.

Fantuan (饭团外卖) covers Los Angeles (one of 9 cities incl. Vancouver, Toronto, New York, LA, Chicago) and calls SF, LA and New York its 'tier 1' US markets; it has an LA Instagram account (@la_fantuan). No public page describes Fantuan supplying, renting or financing rider vehicles in LA.

The earlier agent's statement that 'Fantuan rents e-bikes to its own riders in LA' could not be verified in two Chinese-language and one English search; treat it as unconfirmed until a Fantuan rider-ops contact confirms.

World Journal (2025-12-01): a former Ele.me courier now in LA works Fantuan and other Chinese platforms, does 20-30 orders/day, and rides a Ninebot (九号) electric scooter he shipped from China himself. Evidence that Chinese-platform LA riders self-supply low-cost Chinese e-scooters.

HungryPanda (熊猫外卖) operates in LA (Instagram @hungrypandala, Facebook HungryPandaLA); global rider requirements: 18+, work-eligible visa, vehicle documentation, 'requirements differ by city'; US-specific vehicle rules not published; the company offers rider 'Panda Care Boxes'/rider stations and yellow-black safety rebrand, not vehicles. Partnerships email: business@hungrypanda.co.

JQS Delivery (JQS LA 딜리버리): Koreatown in-house delivery agency since 2010, phone 213-905-0441, website jqsdelivery.com ('No hidden fee delivery food in Ktown LA'); services: restaurant food, personal items, corporate group orders, shipping. Vehicle type, fleet size, owner and street address are NOT published.

LA Joy Quick Service (LA 조이퀵서비스 / LA퀵서비스) is listed as a Koreatown quick-courier business on HeyKorean's Ktown directory; vehicles unverified (Korean 'quick service' in the US is typically car/van based).

Korean-language search for Koreatown scooter/motorcycle delivery agencies returned no LA business advertising scooter fleets; results were Korean-domestic (bunjang, tayota lease). LA Koreatown delivery appears car-based.
Domino's US launched a national e-bike program in 2019 with Rad Power Bikes as exclusive e-bike provider for US franchisees and corporate stores (custom cargo e-bike, 12 large pizzas, 20 mph).

Benzina Zero HAULeR cargo e-bike is 'approved for use within the Domino's Pizza Enterprises network' — DPE is the Australia/NZ/Europe/Japan master franchisee, not Domino's US. No evidence of HAULeR approval for US stores.

Whether Rad Power Bikes still supplies Domino's US after its 2025 financial distress is unverified; LA franchisee 'Delivery Biker' postings (per earlier agent) are bring-your-own-bike, which suggests store-owned e-bikes are not standard in LA.

Spanish-language search for delivery e-bike rentals in Los Angeles returned only tourist rentals (Santa Monica/West Hollywood, Airbnb/Viator) and Whizz NYC content ($49/week in NYC); no LA courier rental operator exists in Spanish-language results.

how_to_reach: DoorDash: email eco-doordash@doordash.com with a one-page LA offer (INNO delivery combo, X% Dasher discount, rental price, 768 Ceres Ave store, UL/SB 1271 battery compliance, Dasher-verification form on hmpbikes.com modeled on dirwinbike.com/pages/delivery-partnerships).

HungryPanda: email business@hungrypanda.co (published partnerships address) in Chinese and English proposing an LA rider-perk program (discounted INNO rental + battery swap at Ceres Ave); ask for LA rider count and vehicle mix.

Fantuan: founder-to-founder Chinese-language approach through the LA city manager (Instagram @la_fantuan / fantuan.ca merchant partnership channel); confirm or refute the rider e-bike rental claim before building a plan on it.
JQS Delivery: call 213-905-0441 (Korean-speaking staff advisable) to learn vehicle mix and driver count; offer 2-3 demo INNOs for a Koreatown route trial.
Domino's LA: identify franchisee entities from jobs.dominos.com posting employer names; approach only if HMP pursues Domino's US vehicle approval (long cycle; low priority).
Uber Eats: no public path; approach via Uber's LA city operations team after DoorDash listing exists.
constraints: Platforms (DoorDash, Uber, Fantuan, HungryPanda) do not buy or lease vehicles; they list partners and pass discounts to riders. Revenue arrives as individual rider purchases/rentals, not POs.

FLASH and Lightning MK.II require CA M1 license, registration and insurance; gig couriers overwhelmingly lack M1, and platforms classify motorcycles as car-tier deliveries. Courier-side demand for FLASH/MK.II is negligible.
LA courier market is car-dominated (~24,000 daily-active couriers, ~740 two-wheel in the core zone per context); Koreatown and SGV in-house delivery appears car-based.
Chinese-platform riders self-supply cheap Chinese e-scooters (Ninebot) at a fraction of INNO's $2,300, so the pitch must be rental/rent-to-own with service, not outright sale.

DoorDash listing likely requires UL 2849/2271-listed batteries (SB 1271), insurance, and an operating store; HMP's SF rental price (~$88-90/week) is ~2x Zoomo/Whizz benchmarks and would need an LA rate near $40-60/week.
No public fleet-size or vehicle data for any Koreatown delivery agency; every count above is an estimate pending site visits.
what_hmp_must_have: A Dasher-style verification form and discount offer (Dirwin template) on hmpbikes.com before emailing eco-doordash@doordash.com.
An LA rental rate card at $40-60/week for INNO (with battery swap) to be competitive with Zoomo/Whizz benchmarks if either enters LA.
Chinese-language rider marketing (Xiaohongshu/WeChat) and a bilingual rider-ops contact for Fantuan/HungryPanda riders.
UL-certified batteries and documentation (SB 1271) and a lithium storage plan at 768 Ceres Ave (2025 CFC section 320).
A 2-3 unit demo/loaner pool for Koreatown and SGV delivery agencies.
Fleet pricing sheet (12-18% off) for 5+ unit buyers, plus a rent-to-own contract template.

realistic_12mo_units.rationale: No confirmed 10-50-unit courier-side buyer exists in LA. Base case assumes a DoorDash Dasher Deals listing plus HungryPanda/Fantuan rider-perk partnerships funnel ~15-20 individual INNO rentals/purchases, and one or two Koreatown/SGV delivery agencies trial 3-5 units each. High case adds a Fantuan rider-vehicle program if the unverified rental claim proves true (10-25 units). Low case is a handful of walk-in riders. Zero FLASH/MK.II units from this segment.

red_flags: The earlier agent's 'Fantuan rents e-bikes to LA riders' claim is unverified after three searches; do not size a plan on it.
Whizz added four cities under its DoorDash partnership in 2025-26 and could enter LA at $129-219/month rent-to-own, undercutting HMP's SF-style pricing; HMP's SF recurring revenue is already falling.
Zoomo's silent LA exit (plans page now NYC-only) suggests LA two-wheel courier rental demand did not support a branded operator.
Koreatown delivery agencies and Domino's LA franchisees show no evidence of two-wheel fleets; counts here are estimates.
Chinese-platform riders import sub-$1,000 e-scooters; INNO at $2,300 sale or ~$380/month rental is a hard sell without financing.
